title: CBSE CLASS 9 — Social Science | Development Economic Indicators
description: Subject-wise test on Development Economic Indicators (Social Science) for CBSE CLASS 9. 50Q.
subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is generally considered the most important attribute for comparing the development of different countries?

options.text: Literacy Rate
options.explanation: While literacy rate is an important indicator, it is not the most important attribute for comparing the development of different countries.

options.text: Infant Mortality Rate
options.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate is an important indicator of a country's health infrastructure, but it is not the most important attribute for comparing the development of different countries.

options.text: Per Capita Income
options.explanation: Per Capita Income is the most important attribute for comparing the development of different countries as it reflects the average income-earning capacity.

options.text: Net Attendance Ratio
options.explanation: Net Attendance Ratio is an important indicator of education, but it is not the most important attribute for comparing the development of different countries.

questions.explanation: Per Capita Income is traditionally used as the primary economic indicator for comparing the development levels of different countries, as it reflects the average income-earning capacity.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: What does HDI stand for?

options.text: Human Development Information
options.explanation: HDI does not stand for Human Development Information.

options.text: Healthy Development Indicator
options.explanation: HDI does not stand for Healthy Development Indicator.

options.text: Human Development Index
options.explanation: HDI stands for Human Development Index, which is a composite statistic of life expectancy, education, and per capita income indicators.

options.text: High Development Indicator
options.explanation: HDI does not stand for High Development Indicator.

questions.explanation: HDI is a composite statistic of life expectancy, education, and per capita income indicators, which are used to rank countries into four tiers of human development.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a public facility?

options.text: Private car
options.explanation: A private car is not a public facility as it is not accessible to all.

options.text: Public transport
options.explanation: Public transport is a public facility as it is accessible to all and is essential for a good quality of life.

options.text: Personal mobile phone
options.explanation: A personal mobile phone is not a public facility as it is not accessible to all.

options.text: Family house
options.explanation: A family house is not a public facility as it is not accessible to all.

questions.explanation: Public facilities are services provided by the government or collectively by the community, accessible to all, and are essential for a good quality of life.

questions.question: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) refers to the number of children who die before the age of ____ per 1000 live births.

options.text: 3 years
options.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate refers to the number of children who die before the age of 1 year, not 3 years.

options.text: 5 years
options.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate refers to the number of children who die before the age of 1 year, not 5 years.

options.text: 1 year
options.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate refers to the number of children who die before the age of 1 year.

options.text: 10 years
options.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate refers to the number of children who die before the age of 1 year, not 10 years.

questions.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is defined as the number of deaths of children under one year of age per 1000 live births.

questions.question: A country has a very high per capita income but also a very high Infant Mortality Rate and low literacy rate. This indicates that:

options.text: The country is highly developed.
options.explanation: A high per capita income does not necessarily mean that a country is highly developed if it has poor health and education indicators.

options.text: The country's income distribution is very equitable.
options.explanation: A high per capita income coupled with poor health and education indicators suggests that the income distribution may not be very equitable.

options.text: Income alone is not a sufficient indicator of development.
options.explanation: High per capita income coupled with poor health and education indicators suggests that income alone is not a sufficient indicator of development.

options.text: Public facilities in the country are excellent.
options.explanation: A high per capita income coupled with poor health and education indicators suggests that public facilities may not be excellent.

questions.explanation: High per capita income coupled with poor health and education indicators suggests that the benefits of income are not reaching all sections of society or are not being invested adequately in public facilities, highlighting that income alone isn't a complete measure of development.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): Public facilities play a crucial role in the human development of a region. Reason (R): States like Kerala have achieved better human development outcomes due to significant investments in public services like health and education, even with moderate per capita income.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason provides a correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is true and provides a correct example of the importance of public facilities.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true and correctly states the importance of public facilities.

questions.explanation: The assertion correctly states the importance of public facilities. The reason provides a concrete example (Kerala) where effective provision of public services has led to higher human development, thus correctly explaining why public facilities are crucial.

questions.question: Sustainable development aims to:

options.text: Maximize current economic growth at any cost.
options.explanation: Sustainable development does not aim to maximize current economic growth at any cost, but rather to balance economic growth with environmental protection and social equity.

options.text: Exploit all natural resources for immediate benefit.
options.explanation: Sustainable development does not aim to exploit all natural resources for immediate benefit, but rather to manage resources responsibly for both current and future generations.

options.text: Meet the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
options.explanation: Sustainable development aims to meet the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

options.text: Focus solely on industrial development.
options.explanation: Sustainable development does not focus solely on industrial development, but rather aims to balance economic growth with environmental protection and social equity.

questions.explanation: Sustainable development is a concept that emphasizes balancing economic growth with environmental protection and social equity, ensuring that resources are managed responsibly for both current and future generations.

questions.question: A state has a Literacy Rate of 85% and a Net Attendance Ratio for classes 1-5 of 70%. Which of the following conclusions can be drawn?

options.text: All children in the state are attending school.
options.explanation: A Net Attendance Ratio of 70% suggests that not all children are attending school.

options.text: The state has achieved universal primary education.
options.explanation: A Net Attendance Ratio of 70% suggests that the state has not achieved universal primary education.

options.text: A significant portion of children might not be attending primary school despite a high general literacy.
options.explanation: A literacy rate of 85% indicates a good level of adult literacy, but a Net Attendance Ratio of 70% suggests that a significant portion of children might not be attending primary school.

options.text: The state's Infant Mortality Rate must be very low.
options.explanation: There is no direct relationship between Literacy Rate, Net Attendance Ratio, and Infant Mortality Rate.

questions.explanation: A literacy rate of 85% indicates a good level of adult literacy, but a Net Attendance Ratio of 70% suggests that a significant portion of children might not be attending primary school despite a high general literacy.

questions.question: Which of the following is generally considered the most common method for comparing the development of different countries?

options.text: Infant Mortality Rate
options.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate is an indicator of health and well-being, but it is not the most common method for comparing the development of different countries.

options.text: Literacy Rate
options.explanation: Literacy Rate is an indicator of education, but it is not the most common method for comparing the development of different countries.

options.text: Per Capita Income
options.explanation: Per Capita Income (PCI) is the total income of the country divided by its total population. It is widely used as a basic indicator for comparing the economic development levels between countries, as it gives an average income per person.

options.text: Net Attendance Ratio
options.explanation: Net Attendance Ratio is an indicator of education, but it is not the most common method for comparing the development of different countries.

questions.explanation: Per Capita Income (PCI) is the total income of the country divided by its total population. It is widely used as a basic indicator for comparing the economic development levels between countries, as it gives an average income per person.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component used to calculate the Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.text: Life expectancy at birth
options.explanation: Life expectancy at birth is a component of HDI, measuring a long and healthy life.

options.text: Mean years of schooling
options.explanation: Mean years of schooling is a component of HDI, measuring knowledge.

options.text: Gross National Income (GNI) per capita
options.explanation: Gross National Income (GNI) per capita is a component of HDI, measuring a decent standard of living.

options.text: Poverty line of the country
options.explanation: The poverty line is not a direct component of HDI calculation.

questions.explanation: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite index measuring average achievement in three basic dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life (measured by life expectancy at birth), knowledge (measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling), and a decent standard of living (measured by GNI per capita in PPP terms). The poverty line is not a direct component of HDI calculation.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: What does the concept of 'sustainable development' primarily aim to achieve?

options.text: Maximizing economic growth at any cost
options.explanation: Sustainable development does not prioritize economic growth at the expense of the environment.

options.text: Utilizing all natural resources as quickly as possible
options.explanation: Sustainable development emphasizes using resources judiciously, not exploiting them rapidly.

options.text: Meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
options.explanation: Sustainable development aims to balance current needs with the long-term well-being of the planet and future generations.

options.text: Prioritizing industrial development over environmental protection
options.explanation: Sustainable development prioritizes environmental protection and responsible use of resources.

questions.explanation: Sustainable development emphasizes balancing current development needs with the long-term well-being of the planet and future generations. It focuses on using resources judiciously and protecting the environment.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of a 'public facility' in the context of development?

options.text: A private car owned by an individual
options.explanation: A private car is not a public facility, as it is owned and used by an individual.

options.text: A government-run school
options.explanation: A government-run school is a public facility, providing education to the community.

options.text: A personal laptop
options.explanation: A personal laptop is not a public facility, as it is owned and used by an individual.

options.text: A branded pair of shoes
options.explanation: A branded pair of shoes is not a public facility, as it is a personal item.

questions.explanation: Public facilities are services or amenities provided by the government or collective efforts of society that are essential for the well-being and development of the entire community. Government-run schools provide education for all citizens and are a classic example of a public facility.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: If Country A has a total income of $250 billion and a population of 50 million, what is its Per Capita Income?

options.text: $5 million

questions.explanation: Per Capita Income (PCI) is calculated by dividing the total income of a country by its total population.

questions.question: Despite having a lower Per Capita Income than Punjab, Kerala has a higher Human Development Index (HDI). What is the most probable reason for this?

options.text: Kerala has a larger industrial sector than Punjab.
options.explanation: The size of the industrial sector does not directly explain the difference in HDI.

options.text: Kerala has invested significantly in public facilities like health and education.
options.explanation: Investment in public facilities like health and education can lead to better human development outcomes.

options.text: Punjab's population is much higher than Kerala's.
options.explanation: Population size does not directly explain the difference in HDI.

options.text: Kerala has a more fertile agricultural land.
options.explanation: The fertility of agricultural land does not directly explain the difference in HDI.

questions.explanation: Kerala's higher HDI despite lower PCI is often attributed to its strong focus and investment in public facilities, particularly in providing accessible and quality education and healthcare services to its population. This leads to better human development outcomes like higher literacy rates and lower infant mortality rates.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** Per capita income is a useful indicator for comparing the economic development of countries. **Reason (R):** It accurately reflects the distribution of income among the population, indicating equity.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason (R) is false, as PCI does not accurately reflect income distribution.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason (R) is false, as PCI does not accurately reflect income distribution.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false because PCI does not reflect income distribution.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Assertion (A) is true, and Reason (R) is false.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true because Per Capita Income (PCI) provides an average measure of income per person and is widely used for economic comparisons. However, Reason (R) is false because PCI is an average and does not reveal how income is distributed among the people. A high PCI can mask significant income inequality within a country.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: A country reports an Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) of 45 per 1000 live births. What does this indicator primarily suggest about the country's development status?

options.text: The country has a very high literacy rate.
options.explanation: IMR is related to health and well-being, not literacy rate.

options.text: The country is experiencing rapid economic growth.
options.explanation: IMR is not directly related to economic growth.

options.text: The country likely has inadequate healthcare facilities and poor living conditions.
options.explanation: A high IMR indicates deficiencies in public health services and poor living conditions.

options.text: The country has a stable political environment.
options.explanation: IMR is not directly related to political stability.

questions.explanation: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is the number of children that die before the age of one year as a proportion of 1000 live births. A high IMR (like 45) indicates deficiencies in public health services, lack of access to proper medical care, poor sanitation, and potentially malnutrition, all of which are critical aspects of human development.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: Based on the given development indicators, which country would be considered more developed from a holistic perspective?

options.text: Country Beta, because it has a higher Per Capita Income.
options.explanation: Higher PCI does not solely determine a country's development status.

options.text: Country Alpha, because it performs better on human development indicators despite lower PCI.
options.explanation: Country Alpha's superior performance in human development indicators makes it more developed from a holistic perspective.

options.text: Both countries are equally developed as they have strengths in different areas.
options.explanation: Country Alpha's overall performance in human development indicators is stronger.

options.text: Neither country is developed, as both have some weaknesses.
options.explanation: Country Alpha's strengths in human development indicators make it more developed from a holistic perspective.

questions.explanation: While Country Beta has a higher Per Capita Income, Country Alpha shows significantly better performance in key human development indicators such as Literacy Rate, Infant Mortality Rate, and Net Attendance Ratio. A holistic view of development considers not just income but also health and education outcomes. Country Alpha's superior social indicators suggest a better quality of life and human development, making it more developed from a comprehensive perspective.
questions.subject: cbse9-sst

questions.question: The statement 'Money in your pocket cannot buy all the goods and services that you may need to live well' highlights the limitations of Per Capita Income as a sole indicator of development. Which of the following best justifies this statement?

options.text: Money can easily buy a pollution-free environment and security.
options.explanation: Money cannot buy all public goods and services, such as a pollution-free environment and security.

options.text: All goods and services are available for purchase in the market.
options.explanation: Not all goods and services, especially public goods, are available for individual purchase.

options.text: Public facilities, a pollution-free environment, and collective security are not individually purchasable with money.
options.explanation: Many essential aspects of a good life require collective provision and societal cooperation, not individual purchase.

options.text: People living in high-income countries always have access to better public facilities.
options.explanation: Access to public facilities is not solely determined by individual income or the income of the country.

questions.explanation: This statement is justified because many essential aspects of a good life, such as a pollution-free environment, protection from infectious diseases (requiring collective action), and a secure, crime-free neighborhood, are not things an individual can buy with money alone. These are often public goods or facilities that require collective provision and societal cooperation, which are not directly reflected by individual income.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common method of measuring the economic development of a country according to the World Bank?

options.text: National Income
options.explanation: National Income is not the most common method used by the World Bank.

options.text: Per Capita Income

options.explanation: Gross Domestic Product is not the most common method used by the World Bank for this purpose.

options.text: Human Development Index

questions.explanation: The World Bank uses Per Capita Income (average income) as the main criterion for classifying countries as rich or poor, making it the most common method for economic development comparison.

questions.question: What does Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) indicate?

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a public facility?

questions.question: Why is average income considered a limited criterion for comparing development among countries?

options.text: It is difficult to calculate accurately for all countries.
options.explanation: While calculation challenges exist, this is not the primary reason average income is a limited criterion.

options.text: It does not account for the total population size.
options.explanation: Average income does account for population size in its calculation.

options.text: It hides disparities in income distribution within a country.
options.explanation: Average income can mask significant inequalities within a country.

options.text: It only includes income from the agricultural sector.
options.explanation: Average income includes income from all sectors, not just agriculture.

questions.explanation: Average income (Per Capita Income) is useful for overall comparison but fails to reveal how income is distributed among the population.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an economic indicator used to measure development?

options.explanation: Per Capita Income measures average income, which can mask disparities between rich and poor within a country.
